claim: Sutskever et al. (2014) use a deep LSTM encoder to map a source sequence into fixed-dimensional representation and a deep LSTM decoder to generate a target sequence
notes: Two LSTMs and variable-length sequences; figures here are independently drawn schematic abstractions.

claim: Sutskever et al. report WMT14 English-to-French test BLEU 34.8 for standalone LSTM, 33.3 for phrase-based SMT baseline, 36.5 for LSTM reranking 1000 SMT candidates
locator: Official NeurIPS abstract; WMT14 English→French, full test BLEU
notes: Reported numbers, not reproduced. 36.5 is reranking combination system, not standalone LSTM. OOV penalty noted for standalone 34.8.

claim: Reversing source words but not target words markedly improved model performance by shortening certain dependencies
locator: Abstract; paper Section 3 and original Figure 1
notes: Observed for original LSTM experiments, not universal recommendation for modern architectures.

claim: Cho et al. (EMNLP 2014) use an RNN encoder-decoder to score phrase pairs as an additional feature in phrase-based statistical machine translation
notes: Do not conflate standalone end-to-end translation with phrase scoring feature.

claim: Bahdanau et al. hypothesize fixed-length context is a bottleneck and propose trainable alignment plus time-varying weighted source annotations
notes: 2014 preprint/ICLR 2015. Article names later Attention as follow-on, not original Sutskever mechanism.

claim: Luong et al. compare global and local attention approaches in neural machine translation
Autoregressive factorization, right-shifted teacher forcing and padding-masked negative log-likelihood used in the article
locator: Conditional probability training objective, Section 2; article Eq 01–04
notes: Formula chain rule and token masking are independently explained, not a claim of exact original code or dataset reproduction.

claim: Simple beam search can choose a different sequence from greedy decoding, and attention weights form a normalized distribution over source positions
locator: Attention method Section 3; original seq2seq inference discussion in Sutskever Section 2
notes: Widget weights and Beam diagram numbers are synthetic. Runnable toy code verifies only the mathematical invariants.

claim: The Transformer replaces recurrence with attention mechanisms while retaining an encoder-decoder organization in its original configuration
notes: Not a property of the 2014 LSTM paper.

claim: In a synthetic three-target four-source attention matrix, each target row sums to one; applying a chosen row to toy one-dimensional encoder values [1,2,3,0] yields an explicit weighted context scalar.
locator: Bahdanau attention mechanism, §3; independent demonstration in article Section 10
notes: All attention matrix entries and scalar annotations are independent teaching choices, not trained alignment scores or a historical reproduction.
